sections.h2: What helps a Gloucester Township house sell quickly?
sections.html:
A fast sale here comes from three things done early: the fire-district certificate, a payoff statement for taxes and loans, and a price tied to what neighboring houses actually sold for. Gloucester Township is in Camden County, the Census Bureau estimates 67,085 residents for July 1, 2025, and the township ranked 22nd among New Jersey's 565 municipalities in the 2020 census.

Owners occupy 73.0 percent of the homes, and the typical owner-occupied value is $277,800. A house that needs work sits next to move-in-ready listings in that market, which is why some owners pick an as-is cash sale and skip the repairs, showings and loan approval that come with a conventional listing.

sections.h2: What should I know about the layout of Gloucester Township?
sections.html:
The township covers 22.95 square miles of land and includes Blackwood, Glendora and Grenloch along with Chews Landing, Erial, Glen Oaks, Lambs Terrace and Turkey Foot. It was formed on June 1, 1695, while the land was part of Gloucester County, and it joined Camden County when that county was created in 1844. Big Timber Creek crosses it on the way to the Delaware River.

Neighbors in Camden County are Hi-Nella, Lindenwold, Magnolia, Pine Hill, Runnemede, Somerdale, Stratford and Winslow Township, and across the line in Gloucester County are Deptford Township and Washington Township. Camden County College's 320-acre campus in Blackwood took its first students in 1968.

  • Blackwood and Glendora: census-designated places with 4,622 and 4,784 residents in 2020.
  • Erial: an unincorporated community that is home to Timber Creek Regional High School.
  • The Atlantic City Expressway corridor, which crosses the southwest part of the township.

sections.h2: Which Gloucester Township figures should guide my price?
sections.html:
State data for 2025 put the average residential tax bill here at $7,920, while the 710 homes sold in the state's study averaged $338,576. The table collects those numbers with the Census Bureau's.

The state lists a 2025 general rate of 4.179 per $100 for the township and an effective rate of 2.703. Average sales ran about $149,000 above the average assessment, so price from recent closings and leave the tax card aside.

sections.h2: Who issues the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate in Gloucester Township?
sections.html:
The fire district serving your street handles it, because the township is split into several fire districts. Fire District No. 4's Bureau of Fire Prevention posts a smoke and carbon monoxide certification application and takes inspection requests by phone or email.

To find your district, search your street address in the township's property tax lookup and read the Special Taxing Districts line on the record. FIRE DISTRICT=F04 means District No. 4. State rules call for the certificate before a one-family or two-family house is sold, and it stays valid for six months from issue, so schedule the inspection close to closing.

The district says alarm requirements can vary with a property's age and layout, and a failed inspection brings a list of fixes and a re-inspection. Ask the township construction office whether any other resale paperwork applies before you list.

sections.h2: How does the Gloucester Township tax office handle a sale?
sections.html:
Quarterly installments come due on the first of February, May, August and November, with the maximum 10-day grace period state law allows. Delinquencies accrue 8 percent a year up to $1,500 and 18 percent beyond that, and the office adds a 6 percent penalty to a balance over $10,000 left open at year end. Current-year taxes still delinquent after November 11 face tax sale before December 30, and payments in that period require cash or certified funds.

The office lists two $250 deductions, one for qualifying seniors and disabled residents and one for veterans. A delay in the tax levy certification stretched the third-quarter 2026 grace period to September 2, 2026, which shows how bill dates can move, so ask for a written payoff figure before closing.

To contest an assessment, file with the Camden County Board of Taxation by 4:00 p.m. on April 1, or May 1 in a town that has done a revaluation. An assessment between $150,000 and $500,000 carries a $25 fee, which covers the township's average residential assessment. Keep paying while the appeal is pending, because skipped payments can get it dismissed.

sections.h2: What will a Gloucester Township seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
The payoff and the state's Realty Transfer Fee are usually the largest items. At or below $350,000 the schedule starts at $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, and the state's own worked example puts the fee on a $325,000 deed at $1,910. The seller pays it when the deed is recorded.

  • Transfer fee, from the state's rate table.
  • Payoff of the mortgage, credit line or tax lien.
  • Certificate fee charged by the fire district.
  • The GIT/REP-3 residency certification attached to the deed.

The Camden County Clerk at 520 Market Street in Camden records deeds and accepts electronic recording. Out-of-state sellers prepay Gross Income Tax of 2 percent of the price or more unless an assurance on the GIT/REP-3 applies.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and buses serve Gloucester Township?
sections.html:
Gloucester Township Public Schools teach prekindergarten through eighth grade in eight elementary schools and three middle schools: Glen Landing, Charles W. Lewis and Ann A. Mullen. Ninth through twelfth graders attend Highland Regional in Blackwood, Timber Creek Regional in Erial or Triton Regional in Runnemede, assigned by address within the Black Horse Pike Regional School District.

In 2010 the township listed 239.44 miles of road, 186.25 of them municipal. The Atlantic City Expressway crosses the southwest corner, Routes 42 and 168 run through the west, and County Routes 534 and 544 cover the center and the northern edge. NJ Transit's 400 bus reaches Philadelphia, and the 403 and 459 serve local trips.

sections.h2: What should a landlord check before selling in Gloucester Township?
sections.html: The township's downloads page carries a Landlord Identity Registration form, so a rental owner should confirm the registration is current before listing. About 27 percent of homes are renter-occupied and typical rent is $1,592, which makes tenant-occupied houses a normal part of the market. The fire certificate also applies to a lease or change of occupancy.

faqs.q: Does Gloucester Township require a resale certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: The required certificate is the smoke and carbon monoxide one, issued through the fire district for your address. Ask the township construction office whether any other resale paperwork applies to your house.

faqs.q: How can I tell which fire district my house is in?
faqs.a: Search your street address in the township's property tax lookup and read the Special Taxing Districts line. F04 means Fire District No. 4.

faqs.q: What are the Gloucester Township tax due dates?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, each with a 10-day grace period. Late balances accrue interest, and taxes still delinquent after November 11 can go to tax sale.

faqs.q: By when must I appeal a Gloucester Township assessment?
faqs.a: By 4:00 p.m. on April 1, or May 1 where the town did a revaluation or reassessment. The Camden County Board of Taxation hears appeals at 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood and offers a summary hearing with no appearance.

faqs.q: May I sell a Gloucester Township house with liens or a foreclosure pending?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale price covers every payoff. Get written figures from each lender and from the tax collector, since tax sale charges add fees beyond the posted tax total.
